project.title: Identification of microtubule associated proteins
project.projectDescription: To find out the identities of microtubule-associated proteins whose abundances are visibly reduced in presence of Taxol. For this experiment, microtubule-associated proteins are pulleddown after treatment with Taxol. Untreated cells are used as a control.
project.sampleProcessingProtocol: HeLa Kyoto cells expressing GFP-tagged β-tubulin proteins from BAC transgenes were grown to near-confluency on two 15-cm cell culture dishes per interaction experiment. DSS solution was prepared fresh in dry DMSO at a concentration of 20 mM concentration. Before crosslinking, cells were washed with ice-cold PBS (pH 8.0) to remove amine-containing culture media and extracellular proteins. DSS solution was added at a final concentration of 5 mM for 30 mins. The reaction was quenched by 10 mM Tris-Cl for 15 mins at room temperature. Cells were collected by scraping and snap frozen in liquid N2. Three replicates were harvested. Cell pellets were lysed with a buffer containing 0.1% NP-40 and subjected to affinity purification using anti-GFP antibodies immobilized on a magnetic beads. Purified proteins were digested sequentially with LysC and trypsin, desalted and subjected to mass spectrometric analysis on an Orbitrap instrument.
project.dataProcessingProtocol: Raw files were processed with MaxQuant to match identified tryptic peptides to human uniprotdatabase. Further identified proteins are qunatified by the label-free qunatification. Proteingroups output of MaxQuant was processed in Perseus (v.1.6.14.0) program with standard procedure.
